newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's second digital TV platform opens September.
newsitem.headline: Spain's second digital TV platform opens September.

text.p: Spain's second digital television platform, Via Digital, will begin commercial operations from September, Chairman Pedro Perez said on Tuesday.

The Via Digital project, in conjunction with Telefonica, RTVE, Televisa, independent television stations and Spanish newspapers and magazines, will offer 35 channels including film, sport and specialised information.
Via Digital is also expected to launch a 24-hour news channel and live broadcasts from parliament.
The company will initially rely on 10 billion pesetas capital but Perez said the entire project will require about 100 billion pesetas investment over the next three years.

The main shareholders are Telefonica (35 percent), RTVE (25.45 percent) and Televisa (25.45 percent). But Perez said said within a short time, no shareholder would hold more than a 25 percent stake in line with Spanish norms.
The company aims to get one million subscribers before the end of the year 2000, the chairman said.
Spain's other digital television platform, CanalSatelite Digital, was launched at the end of January and has 43,000 subscribers.
The operators of the two digital television platforms have clashed over which decoders to use and over soccer broadcast rights.

Regarding the decoder, Perez said his company will promote the so-called "multicrypt" system, the only system recognised as valid under Spanish law if there is no accord of compatibility with the system used by CanalSatelite Digital.
